notes: The PDF pages show only pictures and the parts list. Part type names come from the LEGO design ids, not from Element IDs, so they are my best guess.

The inventory pages list design ids with a colour suffix, not full Element IDs. Types are therefore lego-<design id> and the colour is in props. Catalogue entries were reused where the design id matched (302301, 302201, 302226).

Fix for the single-use port errors: every connection now uses its own stud or anti-stud port. The new part types have enough numbered ports, for example b1 stud.1 to stud.6, b6 anti-stud.1 and anti-stud.2, b20 anti-stud.1 and anti-stud.2, and side-stud.1 and side-stud.2 on the white side-stud bricks. The pink pieces b32 and b42 use two anti-stud ports because they sit on two studs each.

Exact stud positions are hard to read from the small isometric pictures, so some joins in steps 2 to 17 are inferred. I put the ears (b34 to b37) on the pink plate and on plates at the top of the head.
Piece counts match the inventory: 53 pieces, of which 47 are single ids and 6 are in the 3x repeat.
The 3x repeat in step 17 is a white curved slope on a white 1x2 plate. Its three copies attach to side-stud.2 of three different head bricks (b24, b25, b26).
Step 16 uses one more slope (b47) on a plate stack (b43, b44) as the foot, with a round piece (b39) at its end.
Step 18 shows the pink heart (b42) on the panda's lap, held by two plates with holes (b45, b46).
